title: Chloride–bicarbonate geometry does not establish incremental digit-symbol prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: A source-specified chloride-by-bicarbonate product failed an incremental DSST prediction test across independently recruited NHANES2011–2012 and2013–2014 samples (1289/1505 adults60+). Against flexible standard chemistry and demographic predictors, weighted MSE gain was −0.066461 score² (−0.03965%); two-sample stratified-PSU full-pipeline bootstrap95% interval [−1.153023,0.680793]. A better-performing posthoc linear baseline gave a small positive product gain, limiting the conclusion to the registered model comparison. This negative cross-sectional result does not establish equivalence, causality, or clinical utility.
